saints.name: St. Kilian
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: An Irish missionary bishop who won Franconia for Christ and died a martyr at Würzburg…
biography: Kilian was an Irishman, born about the year 640, it is said, to noble parents near Mullagh in what is now County Cavan. Fired by the Irish custom of pilgrimage for Christ, he crossed the sea with eleven companions and in 686 stood before Pope Conon in Rome, receiving from him a mission and episcopal consecration.

With two companions who remained — the priest Colman and the deacon Totnan — he made the fortress town of Würzburg his seat and preached through East Franconia and Thuringia, converting Duke Gozbert together with a great part of his still pagan people.

When Kilian told the duke that his marriage to Geilana, his brother's widow, was unlawful, she took revenge: while Gozbert was absent, her soldiers beheaded the three missionaries, about the year 689. Burchard, Würzburg's first bishop, enshrined their relics in the cathedral he built on the spot. Kilian is honored as the apostle of Franconia and patron of Würzburg, where his skull and those of his companions are venerated still.
saints.knownFor: Evangelizing Franconia and his martyrdom at Würzburg.
